cases.name: a removed log group with skip_destroy = true is forgotten, not deleted: the provider leaves it and its logs in AWS (source case: beneficiary-fhir-data 75e2cde9d)
a removed log group with skip_destroy = false is still a deletion that loses the logs
skip_destroy on a resource type that does not support it does not stop a deletion

a module for_each over a map with literal keys and partly unknown values keeps its keys when a resource over the same map is evaluated first and the map reads another module, so moved blocks into its instances match (source case: beneficiary-fhir-data 01fc5569f)
two unknown values that differ only in the data source behind them are an unknown update, not a possible replacement (source case: storage-service 5c47edf85, a backend role change)
two unknown values that differ only in the expression behind them are an unknown update (source case: cztack 50192f96a, a role name)
two unknown values with the same known text around them that differ only in origin are an unknown update (source case: forms-terraform 5e27579a2)
an unknown value that now reads a different resource is still a possible replacement
an unknown value whose expression changed and whose resource is replaced is still a possible replacement
two unknown values whose known text differs are still a possible replacement
an edit to a partly unknown jsonencode() result inside a string template shows as a change (source case: opg-use-an-lpa ECS container definitions, probe rs-template)
a partly unknown jsonencode() result inside a string template that does not change is no change
a sensitive value inside a partly unknown jsonencode() result in a string template is never printed
deleting an API Gateway stage is reviewed: the API stops serving that stage, and the unchanged deployment does not recreate it (source case: storage-service 130cdbfd9)
deleting a load balancer listener is reviewed: the load balancer stops accepting connections on its port
deleting a CloudFront distribution is reviewed
a rename hint pairs each deleted instance with the created instance of the same key (source case: beneficiary-fhir-data eccc5da4e)
an unknown value read from a remote state that now reads another state key is still a possible replacement
